Preface
Presented herewith is Book III of Deva Keralam (Chandra Kala Nadi) from sloka No. 1998 to
5774 (1.6. 3796 slokas) - the portion compiled by Venkatesa.
The arrangement of the book goes thus:
Sloka No. 1 to 2718 by Achyuta in Book I.
Sloka No. 2719 to 3407 of Achyuta, and sloka No.1 to 1997 of Venkatesa in Book II.
Sloka No. 1998 to 5774 by Venkatesa in Book III.
These 3 volumes put together have a total of 9181 slokas in all (3407 by Achyuta and 5774 by
Venkatesa) for which complete English translation has been provided by me.
As the discerning reader understands, the work covers two areas of delineation. A particular
space of rising degree called Nadiamsa is used to depict a series of events to occur in the native’s life,
one of the subtle techniques of handling a horoscope. On the other hand, countless general principles
are enumerated on the lines done by popular series of text-books like Parasara Hora, Phala Deepika,
Saravali, Jataka Parijata and Sarvartha Chintamani dealing with natal horoscopy including dasa
effects, transits and the like. In some cases, general principles that do not consider Nadiamsa
technique are incorporated in the Nadiamsa reading. To avoid confusion to the reader, these have
been separated by me in the translation, as far as possible. Further, these have been more clearly
sorted out in the index given at the end of the present volume. The index now given embraces all the
3 parts.
As the reader knows, each sign has 150 Nadiamsas and the 12 signs have a total of 1800
Nadiamsas. It is not humanly possible to bring out a work dealing with all the 1800 Nadiamsas. To
the extent possible, the authors Achyuta and Venkatesa, gathered a‘large amount of information on
this most subtle division. An intelligent reader can multiply the use of a Nadiamsa four-fold keeping
in mind the three classifications of the 12 zodiacal signs into movable, fixed and common signs.
For example, a rule given for a certain Nadiamsa for Aries can be suitably extended to the other
three movable signs, viz. Cancer, Libra and Capricorn. Similarly the four fixed signs Taurus, Leo,
Scorpio and Aquarius can be brought under the second category. The three dual signs Gemini, Virgo,
Sagittarius and Pisces form part of the 3rd group. While doing so, the involvement of planets should
be judiciously understood. This is because the same planet plays a different role for each sign
ascending.
The text excels in merits in tactfully combining the usage of Vimsottari dasa and Kala Chakra
dasa. So also in applying transits with reference to the signs caused by certain Navamsa positions.
Many such rare techniques are available in this wonderful work. One who uses such techniques
frequently will be able to issue successful predictions.
I sincerely believe that the reader will find our present efforts useful and forgive me for my
shortcomings if any.
Mr. Narinder Sagar of Sagar Publications deserves special thanks for undertaking the task of
bringing out this voluminous work considering the huge amount of money that the production of a
book of this size requires.

of births relating to the 4 castes (i.e. Brahmin,

should be done only after her attaining puberty.

of) seven past generations will be burnt. So had
been said by Manu and Parasara. The science of
astrology also declares such effects. A girl of 8 is
known as Kanya, of 9 Rohini, of 10 Gauri and
above 10 Rajasvala (who attained her puberty and
is fit for marriage). For Brahmins, Kshatriyas and
Vaisyas, the giving away of a Kanya is important
(i. e. is recommended). For Soodra, marrriage is
allowed of a Rohini or Gauri. If there be obstacles
in performing the marriage of a son or daughter,.
worship of a Sumangali (a female whose husband
is alive), Maha Lakshmi and Gauri (i.e. Lakshmi
and Parvati) should be done as prescribed by
Sastras. Lakshmi and Parvati should be offered
Abhisheka (ritual bath) with milk and turmeric.

again and again), with purity. Then the hurdles will
be removed and marriage will take place.

per Sastras. More suh information can be found in

Notes: This portion attempts to instruct us on

Moon. These and the 36 Chandra Velas are welldiscussed coherently in texts like Phala Deepika
and by Pandit late M. R. K. Bhat in his work,
Essentials of Horary Astrology. But in our present

so that my job is completed in a satisfactory

Chandra Kriya (Moon's actions): One Nakshatra is 13° 20' or 800' of arc. Divide 800 by 60
and find out in what part of such a portion is the
Moon placed. That will be Chandra Kriya.
Example: Say the Moon is 2° 40’ of Aswini, i.e.
160th minute of longitude in Aswini. 160 divided
by 60 yields the 3rd Chandra Kriya. The result
mentioned for the 3rd Kriya will apply to the
Moon's particular position.
Also see slokas 2570 - 2578 infra for effects of
Chandra Kriyas. Our text gives another methd of
Chandra Kriya which are five per sign, and 60 in all
for 12 signs, which are found from sloka 2579
onward.
Chandra Avasthas (Moon's states): There
are 12 specific Avasthas for the Moun which
should be found out by dividing 800 by 12. In
which of the 12th part is the Moon located in that
particular Nakshatra should thus be known which
will tell of Chandra Avastha.
(Similarly for Chandra Vela, the divisor is 36
as there are 36 Chandra Velas, or the Moon's
periods.)
These can be used in respect of birth horoscope,
query horoscopes, Muhurta etc.

existence of blemish in the family of brothers (of
the native).

with other men. :

5740 - 57491/2: Planets Described: (a) The
Sun has a symmetric body. He is a king and has
other names, viz. Dyumani and Divakara. Heis fire
(personified), fierce and causes happiness to the
world. He is the ruler of bile ("Peeta” reads as
"Pitta" in another version which is used in the
rendering), quadrupeds and the direction east. His
hue is golden.
(b) The Moon is strong in the nights. She is fair
in complexion and is the ruler of north-west. She
is perishable by nature (i. e. she wanes periodically), is handsome (when waxing), sagely, phlegmatic, is watery (Jit. has the form of water), has a
body subject to decrease and increase, is learned,
soft-spoken and has attractive eyes.
(c) Mars resembles fire. He is sharp and is
(known as) "Kona". The direction south is ruled by
him. He is a youth, of royal scion and has a square
body. He is known as "Vakra" (or crooked) and has
blood-red complexion. His eyes are fierce and his
belly depressed.
(d) Mercury resides in villages, is handsome,
courageous and has a composition of all the three
humours (viz. wind, phlegm and bile). He is
learned, dark in complexion, the lord of the northern direction, and fond of music and all kinds of
tastes. He is Tara's son, highly intelligent, courageous, and fond of jokes.

280 Deva Keralam
(€) Jupiter is a Brahmin, winner of senses,
attached to performing sacrificial rites, highly phlegmatic, sweet, knower of feelings (or truth) and very
righteous. He rules gold, is of middle age, follows
Vedic path and is the lord of north-east.
(f) The planet Venus is handsome, is formed of
water ("Jalamaya"), passionate, fond of love and
is a middle-aged female. She is a Brahmin, is the
lord of south-east, and fond of music. Her body is
resplendent. She lives in islands and has charming
eyes.
(g) Saturn is fond of Soodra females and is the
lord of the western direction. He is harmful in
disposition, lame, old and has a "stout" body.
(0) Rahu'shead is like that of a snake. Heis like
Saturn and wanders during nights (like demons).
Ketu is equal to Mars, is phlegmatic, of variegated
hue and is fikle-minded.
Notes: (b) The word "Kshara" relating to the
Moon has various meanings like medicinal salt,
molasses, perishable, mutable and dissoluble. Since
the Moon wanes in the dark fortnight, the meaning
chosen in the rendering may be treated as appropriate although this quality is reflected in the words
("Kshaya Vriddhi Tanuh".)
(c) The word "Kona" for astrological purposes
has twomeanings. Itisa synonym of Saturnas well
as Mars. Most of the texts however denote only
Saturn by this term while Mars is never indicated.
(f) Although it is a tradition in English translations to use masculine pronoun "he" for Venus, in
this portion "she" is used as an exception to remain
in line with the context.
(h) Rahu is compared to Saturn and Ketu to
Mars, in line with the misused popular adage -
"Sanivadrahu kujvatketu". The comparison is
restricted to the general disposition of the two
nodes and does not allow swapping Rahu with
Saturn and Ketu with Mars for every convenient
purpose on the earth.

5750 - 5753. Rasi Divisions: (a) Thirty degrees
constitute a Rasi (Jit. ascendant).
(b) Half of it is called Hora.
(c) Drekkana is a third of the sign.
(d) Dvadasamsa is one twelfth of a sign.
(e) Trimsamsa is constituted by thirtieth parts.
(f) The drekkana distribution should in order be
done thus: (to) the lords of the Ist, 5th and 9th in
case of movable signs, the lords of the 9th, Ist and
5th in case of immovable signs, and the 5th, 9th and
the Ist (in case of dual signs).
(g) For positions in Aries, Leo and Sagittarius
count from Aries. For Capricom, Taurus and Virgo
count from Capricorn. For Libra, Aquarius and
Gemini, count from Libra. For Cancer, Scorpio
and Pisces, count from Cancer. (Thus are the
Navamsa distribution to be understood.)
Notes: In these verses, Rasi, Hora, Drekkana,
Trimsamsa, Dvadasamsa and Navamsa calculations are casually touched. The reader is already
aware of these in a fuller measure. Yet clarifications on two points are necessary as under.
(a) The word "ascendant" should not be misinterpreted that the ascendant is always 30 degrees in
length irrespective of interruption by another sign,
and that no Bhava divisions be made with the help
of the meridian as taught by the likes of Parasara
and Sripathi. Our author just took some liberty and
used the word "ascendant" which means a sign.
(d) The drekkana distribution suggested is partially different from what we already know. Incase
of immovable and dual signs, an unknown concept
is introduced. Serious probe is a must whether we
so far know the right thing. According to this text,
for example, in Taurus, a fixed sign, the 3 decanates
are in order ruled by Saturn (Capricorn), Venus
(Taurus) and Mercury (Virgo) and not Venus (Taurus), Mercury (Virgo) and Saturn (Capriorn). In
case of a dual sign, for example Gemini, the three
decanates are ruled by Venus (Libra), Aquarius
(Saturn) and Gemini (Mercury) instead of traditionally known rulers Mercury (Gemini), Venus
(Libra) and Saturn (Aquarius).

यस्तद्वेति स तत्त्ववित् स च गुनिर््रह्याहमयः कालवित् ॥५७७४ ॥
5774. (In the word "Kaala" - काठ - meaning
time), the letter "Kaa" - का - is the reason for the
three worlds, while the other letter "La" - ठक -
stands for Great Dissolution. The Matras (one Guru
and two Laghus, equalling three Laghus) denote
the three Benefactors (Brahma, Vishnu and
Mahesvara). Brahma is of the nature of Kaala. i. e.
he is himself Kaala. Knowing of Kaala ever leads
to attainment of Punya or merits. One who knows
of it is the knower of Tatva, is a sage and appellation of Brahma
